title: Orson Welles and Citizen Kane
subject: art
description: At **25 years**, **Orson Welles** directs *Citizen Kane* (**1941**). The film invents a new language: depth of field, flashbacks and investigation into a mysterious word, Rosebud.

hero.hook: A 25-year-old prodigy films a press mogul and invents modern cinema.

blocks.text: For decades, critics have ranked *Citizen Kane* (**1941**) among the greatest films in history. Its director, **Orson Welles**, is only **25 years old**. The film chronicles the life of newspaper mogul Charles Foster Kane and asks a simple question: can you really know a man?
Beyond the plot, Welles invents a new language. He mixes silent and speaking techniques to talk about power, solitude and memory.

sections.title: The prodigy who gets all the rights

blocks.text: **George Orson Welles** first established himself in the theater, then on the radio. On **October 30, 1938**, he adapts *The War of the Worlds*. By imitating a fake newscast, he makes people believe in an extraterrestrial invasion. Part of America is panicking. Suddenly, Hollywood wants it.

blocks.caption: 1938: Welles terrorizes America with a false radio report.

blocks.text: , a large studio in difficulty, offers Welles a rare contract: total freedom of subject and , that is to say the right to decide alone on the [[Final Cut]]. [[RKO Pictures]]
In Hollywood, such power for a beginner is almost unheard of. Welles took advantage of this to control everything: script, casting, images, sound.

sections.title: Depth of field changes the look

blocks.text: With **cinematographer Gregg Toland**, Welles refuses classic blurred backgrounds. They impose : everything remains sharp, from the foreground to the background. Several actions can be played at the same time in the same frame, without cutting. [[Depth of field (deep focus)]]

blocks.caption: In Citizen Kane, each shot tells several things at once.

blocks.text: Welles also often films from a low angle, with the camera positioned low, to magnify the characters and accentuate their power. The ceilings become visible. The space speaks as much as the dialogues.

The film begins with the ending: Kane dies alone in his palace, . Its last word is **“Rosebud”**. A journalist investigates. Through flashbacks, friends and enemies tell conflicting versions of the same man. [[Xanadu]]

Welles rejects simple biography. For some, Kane is an idealist. For others, a tyrant. The viewer puts the pieces together, without ever obtaining a single truth. The mystery of Rosebud remains an elegant lure: a key too small to unlock a lifetime.

events.title: Citizen Kane
events.detail: Release of the film, immediate commercial failure.

blocks.text: *Citizen Kane* proved that a film could be an investigation into power and memory. Its clear images, its flashbacks and its freedom of editing invented a modernity that cinema is still exploring.
